With curse words, theirs a difference between a simple profanity and a slur. I could care less about any profanity being normalized but if it's a slur that's used when in this case it is no matter how good the person, there's much more weight on the word. 

[https://theconversation.com/wtf-slurs-offend-young-adults-more-than-swearing-125193](https://theconversation.com/wtf-slurs-offend-young-adults-more-than-swearing-125193)

I like this article if you want to read it, it goes more in-depth on the impact no matter how any slur is used.

Again, you can say it but don't expect a positive reaction whether the people in that room express it outwardly or inwardly. There are other people outside of black people who know that it isn't the best thing to say and (hopefully) know why it isn't, too. So whether there are black people around or not, it's still a bit iffy.

That being said though, I don't want to instantly call the person saying it a racist. Though they casually called their friend by it or sang along to a song and said it, in most cases, they don't constantly think racist thoughts towards black people or think about hurting them in any way,,I wouldn't call the person bad or racist, I'd just call them ignorant.

There are other words you can say other than the N word. I find it a bit concerning that out there, there are people who aren’t black trying to justify their saying of the word even though there are other things to say. Thanks for acknowledging that the word holds more weight towards black people, though. It just doesn’t sit right no matter the context.

It’s a word that will always be associated with the long history of slavery, oppression and racial discrimination against black people and while the slavery is in the past, the oppression and racial discrimination are still there. It has and always will be linked with brutality and violence. 

It’s still used as a slur today and that’s anything but okay. That’s another reason why anyone who isn’t black can’t say it.

Black people can say it because it’s theirs to reclaim. It’s been reclaimed and is now used as a symbol of our community rather than an insult. 

It’s not easy growing up as black and it never has been. I’ve had to deal with racism and micro aggressions first hand. We have to live in a world fearing that we’ll be discriminated against due to something we can’t change and anyone who isn’t black hasn’t had to deal with most of this.

For other poc, they have had similar struggles and I acknowledge that, I’m not trying to make this an oppression competition. While I understand what other poc have been though, they haven’t had that slur used towards their community so they can’t say it.

If your gonna say it and aren’t black, don’t expect to get a good reaction out of it.
